section_summary: This section covers U.S. policy on expanding Japanese fishing grounds, disputes over fishing limits and vessel seizures, and plans to inspect Japanese fishing vessels. It also documents Japanese Antarctic whaling, including catches, observers’ reports, and a proposal for three fleets in 1949–1950. Several policy papers and despatches appear with separate enclosures or duplicate copies.

subfiles.title: Current fisheries statistical bulletin, concluding pages
subfiles.about: Reports fisheries landings and trade in Great Britain, Canada, Norway, Denmark, and Newfoundland.
subfiles.summary: The concluding bulletin pages compare postwar fish landings and discuss Canadian herring, Norwegian herring and cod, Danish catches, and Newfoundland salted cod stocks. They end with conversion factors and table symbols.

subfiles.title: Comments on SANACC 99/10 and Japanese fishing expansion
subfiles.about: Evaluates proposed amendments to U.S. policy on expanding Japanese fishing grounds.
subfiles.summary: Allison prefers an immediate decision on southern expansion. If that is impracticable, he supports SANACC 99/8 as an interim measure, with detailed SCAP assurances on conservation and possible inspection by patrol vessels.

subfiles.title: Handling the SANACC fishing paper in the FEC
subfiles.about: Describes preparation and clearance of a fishing policy proposal for the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.summary: Flory will draft an FEC statement once SANACC acts; Chapman wishes to attend committee meetings.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of SANACC 99/11
subfiles.about: Forwards SANACC 99/11 for State Department information.
subfiles.summary: Wilds forwards the policy paper and highlights two recommendations.

subfiles.title: Instructions to the U.S. member of the Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.to: United States Member, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Authorizes presentation of a Japanese fishing policy and accompanying statement.
subfiles.summary: The U.S. member may present the policy, seek its acceptance, and accept changes that preserve its intent.

subfiles.title: Policy with respect to fishing and aquatic industries in Japan
subfiles.about: Sets out proposed U.S. policy for Japanese fishing, conservation, and fleet reparations.
subfiles.summary: The proposal permits SCAP to expand Japanese fishing, requires consultation with directly concerned countries and compliance with conservation agreements, and reserves decisions on the fleet’s final size and reparations.

subfiles.title: Proposed statement for presentation to the Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Describes a planned U.S. response if the Commission fails to approve a fishing policy by January 15, 1949.
subfiles.summary: The United States would notify SCAP that it sees no objection to a specified eastward and southward expansion.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of policy proposal and statement
subfiles.about: Sends the proposal and presentation statement adopted following SANACC 99/11.
subfiles.summary: Keyes explains that wording on countries’ direct concern was adjusted for presentation to the Commission.

subfiles.title: Instructions to the U.S. member of the Far Eastern Commission, second copy
subfiles.to: United States Member, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Authorizes presentation and negotiation of the U.S. fishing policy.
subfiles.summary: A second copy directs the member to seek approval and accept changes consistent with the proposal.

subfiles.title: Fishing and aquatic industries policy, second copy
subfiles.about: Repeats the proposed U.S. policy on Japanese aquatic industries.
subfiles.summary: It addresses fishing expansion, consultation, conservation agreements, fleet size, and reparations.

subfiles.title: Proposed FEC statement, second copy
subfiles.about: Repeats the proposed statement on fishing area expansion if FEC agreement fails.
subfiles.summary: It specifies a January 15 deadline and geographic boundary for expansion.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of SANACC 99/11 to Tokyo
subfiles.to: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Sends SANACC 99/11 to the political adviser for information.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary encloses the U.S. policy on Japanese fishing and other aquatic industries.

subfiles.title: Amendment of the authorized Japanese fishing and whaling area
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Explains a corrected Hokkaido boundary description in SCAPIN 1033/1.
subfiles.summary: The amendment defines a point near Nemuro Strait and Cape Nosappu to clarify the authorized boundary amid Soviet seizures of Japanese vessels.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1033/1: Area authorized for Japanese fishing and whaling
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Amends the geographic boundary of authorized Japanese fishing and whaling.
subfiles.summary: The directive restates the boundary, including its clarified course off eastern Hokkaido.

subfiles.title: Japanese fishing policy and direct concern
subfiles.about: Explains conservation wording, direct concern, and Philippine objections to fishing area expansion.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum describes revised FEC language and possible consultations over an area near Philippine islands.

subfiles.title: Guidance for discussions near the Batan Islands, draft
subfiles.to: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Supplies proposed U.S. high seas conservation policy for SCAP discussions with Philippine representatives.
subfiles.summary: The draft asks that SCAP receive guidance if a conservation zone near the Philippines is discussed.

subfiles.title: Guidance for discussions near the Batan Islands, revised copy
subfiles.to: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Repeats guidance concerning proposed Japanese fishing expansion near the Batan Islands.
subfiles.summary: The revised copy requests delivery of the U.S. high seas conservation policy to SCAP headquarters.

subfiles.title: Soviet complaints about Japanese vessels near Sakhalin and the Kurils
subfiles.about: Reports a Soviet claim that Japanese vessels violated Soviet territorial waters.
subfiles.summary: Sebald notes that the Soviet member insists the issue concerns territorial waters, rather than only SCAP’s authorized fishing area. He suspects the correspondence is intended to advance Soviet territorial claims and requests any pertinent guidance.

subfiles.title: Soviet member’s letter on alleged territorial-water violations
subfiles.about: Demands measures against Japanese fishing vessels allegedly entering Soviet territorial waters.
subfiles.summary: Derevyanko rejects a reply framed around SCAP fishing limits and repeats his territorial-water complaint.

subfiles.title: Reply concerning Soviet fishing-vessel complaints
subfiles.to: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Provides guidance on answering Soviet complaints without acknowledging territorial claims.
subfiles.summary: The Department permits further replies that avoid expressing U.S. views on sovereignty.

subfiles.title: Request for SCAP fisheries reports
subfiles.about: Asks how the American Tunaboat Association can receive SCAP fisheries bulletins.
subfiles.summary: Cary requests placement on a mailing list for reports about fishing in Japan.

subfiles.title: Reply to the American Tunaboat Association
subfiles.about: Explains how the association may receive reproduced SCAP fisheries reports.
subfiles.summary: Chapman refers Cary’s request to the Fish and Wildlife Service for the appropriate mailing list.

subfiles.title: Reported Chinese law concerning Japanese fishing outside the authorized area
subfiles.about: Reports a Chinese law said to authorize seizure of Japanese fishing vessels on the high seas.
subfiles.summary: Sebald recounts earlier Chinese protests and vessel seizures, including a fatal sinking near Zhoushan Island. His mission maintains that SCAP alone enforces its high seas fishing limits and asks the Chinese Mission to investigate the reported law.

subfiles.title: Ta Kung Pao report of Chinese emergency fishing-vessel law
subfiles.about: Prints a reported Chinese law for confiscating Japanese vessels fishing beyond SCAP limits.
subfiles.summary: The seven articles define the prohibited area, call for confiscation of vessels, gear and catches, and set procedures for recording seizures and deporting crews.

subfiles.title: Request to investigate reported Chinese fishing-vessel law
subfiles.about: Questions the reported Chinese power to seize Japanese vessels outside the authorized fishing area.
subfiles.summary: The Diplomatic Section reiterates SCAP’s responsibility for enforcing high seas fishing limits and asks whether the reported Chinese law was promulgated.

subfiles.title: Status of Japanese fishing policy on Keyes’s departure
subfiles.about: Reviews unresolved Trust Area fishing expansion and Philippine objections.
subfiles.summary: Keyes advises waiting for the Army to raise Trust Area expansion and notes uncertain FEC prospects and Philippine negotiations.

subfiles.title: Natural Resources Section plan for Japanese fishery inspection
subfiles.about: Transmits a SCAP study proposing Japanese vessels to monitor compliance with fishing limits.
subfiles.summary: The proposal would use eleven vessels outside the authorized fishing area. The Diplomatic Section concurs subject to calling the operation inspection and informing concerned Allied missions.

subfiles.title: Staff study on enforcing SCAPIN 1033
subfiles.about: Recommends a Japanese vessel system with Allied oversight to detect fishing-limit violations.
subfiles.summary: The study reports 78 violations involving 127 boats but only three convictions. It proposes Japanese vessels, occasional U.S. naval observers, routine military sightings, financing, and radio equipment.

subfiles.title: Proposed SCAP directive on Japanese fishery patrol operations
subfiles.doc_type: draft directive and note for record
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Sets conditions for an eleven-vessel Japanese patrol and records supporting enforcement measures.
subfiles.summary: The draft requires vessel markings, a ten-mile distance from foreign coasts, no fishing by patrol vessels, naval voyage authorization, and room for a SCAP representative. Its note reviews violations, proposed radio installations and penalties, costs, and the aim of avoiding any implication about sovereignty or fishing rights.

subfiles.title: Fourth Japanese Antarctic whaling expedition, duplicate opening and stray continuation
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Introduces a proposal for three Japanese Antarctic whaling fleets; the following page appears to be a misplaced continuation from another despatch.
subfiles.summary: Page 455 duplicates the opening of the May 5 whaling despatch at page 472. Page 456 is a misfiled, damaged continuation referring to Far Eastern Commission preparation and criticism of rearmament.

subfiles.title: Catch at halfway point of Japanese Antarctic whaling expedition
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits a press release on the 1948–1949 whaling expedition’s catch.
subfiles.summary: The expedition had caught 490 blue whale units amid scarce whales and poor weather.

subfiles.title: Whaling expedition radios halfway report
subfiles.about: Reports catches and production from two Japanese Antarctic whaling fleets.
subfiles.summary: The fleets caught 654 whales and processed oil and meat; the catch trailed the prior season.

subfiles.title: Letter from Yaichiro Okada
subfiles.about: Requests State Department review before sending a fisheries leaflet to Yaichiro Okada.
subfiles.summary: Wright encloses Okada’s letter and Fishery Leaflet No. 233 for possible transmission.

subfiles.title: Study of whale migration by marking whales
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits material on a Japanese whale-marking research program.
subfiles.summary: The damaged despatch introduces the enclosed request to the Soviet member and related release.

subfiles.title: Request for Soviet cooperation in whale-marking study
subfiles.to: Office of the Soviet Member, Allied Council for Japan
subfiles.about: Requests data and recovered marking darts from whales caught by Soviet whalers.
subfiles.summary: Japan’s Fisheries Agency will mark whales near the Bonin Islands and Japanese coasts to study migration. SCAP asks Soviet authorities to return recovered darts with catch details, since marked whales may travel toward Kamchatka, Sakhalin, Korea, or Taiwan.

subfiles.title: Request to declassify fisheries conservation data
subfiles.about: Asks whether data on Japan’s fishing conservation program can be shared with the American fishing industry.
subfiles.summary: The damaged letter seeks declassification of Colonel Levy’s information for industry use.

subfiles.title: Australian observer’s comments on Japanese Antarctic whaling
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits Kenneth Coonan’s favorable report on the Nissin Maru.
subfiles.summary: The despatch emphasizes Coonan’s finding of efficient operations and no waste or regulatory violations.

subfiles.title: Kenneth Coonan’s letter from the Nissin Maru
subfiles.about: Assesses the Nissin Maru’s whaling operations during the 1948–1949 season.
subfiles.summary: Coonan praises the crew’s efficiency and describes catch and processing rates. He and Major Crombie observed no waste or violations, and he credits controls on killing with keeping carcasses fresh.

subfiles.title: Status of Formosa and the Kurile Islands
subfiles.about: Requests clarification of a reported State Department statement on the islands’ disposition.
subfiles.summary: Sebald links the Kuril sovereignty issue to Soviet seizures of Japanese fishing vessels and asks for the full statement and instructions.

subfiles.title: Formosa disposition must await treaty
subfiles.about: Reports Michael McDermott’s statement that Formosa and the Kurils await a peace treaty.
subfiles.summary: McDermott says the final disposition of both island areas is subject to a Japanese peace treaty.

subfiles.title: Steering Committee position on fishing and aquatic industries
subfiles.about: Recommends U.S. changes to a proposed FEC fishing policy.
subfiles.summary: Support SC-271/10 with a Canadian wording change and deletion of one sentence and paragraph six.

subfiles.title: Tokyo airgram on a third Antarctic whaling fleet
subfiles.about: Reports SCAP’s anticipated three-fleet Japanese Antarctic whaling proposal.
subfiles.summary: The damaged airgram indicates support for considering a third fleet on food needs and Japan’s whaling record; page 471 contains only stray OCR text.

subfiles.title: Fourth Japanese Antarctic whaling expedition
subfiles.about: Transmits and supports a SCAP proposal for three Japanese whaling fleets in 1949–1950.
subfiles.summary: Huston argues that three fleets could supply food and oil, take an acceptable share of the international quota, and save U.S. funds. He notes likely Allied objections to the added fleet and says SCAP will proceed unless Washington requests changes.

subfiles.title: Internal assessment of the proposed third whaling fleet
subfiles.about: Recommends concurrence with the three-fleet proposal while assessing likely Allied opposition.
subfiles.summary: The writer considers Japan’s proposed share fair and recommends that SCAP seek three fleets, with the response of other countries then assessed. Page 475 is an illegible continuation fragment.

subfiles.title: Natural Resources Section study on three Japanese Antarctic whaling fleets
subfiles.about: Recommends authorizing three Japanese fleets for the 1949–1950 Antarctic whaling season.
subfiles.summary: The opening page cites Japan’s food and oil shortages, prior expedition output, U.S. savings, and an expected 75,000 metric tons of products from three fleets. The study continues beyond this section.
